newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures rise from mixed opening.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures rise from mixed opening.

text.p: IMM currency futures rose to the plus side from mixed levels seen near the outset of holiday-lightened session that brokers expected to stay quiet and choppy.
Yen lagged after its early decline, still pressured by spillover from problems battering Southeast Asian currencies, technicals and crosses with higher-yielding currencies.

The troubles that have slammed the Indonesian rupiah, Malaysian ringgit and Thai baht underscored the potential ripple effect that declines in those units could have on Japanese multinational companies' efforts, analysts said.

In particular, Japanese automakers and computer firms, many of which have large manufacturing facilities in countries such as Thailand, are expected to feel the impact of the drop in the Southeast Asian currencies as they make day-to-day decisions such as where to make a product or obtain parts, said Marc Chandler with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
He also likened Japan's predicament to that of the United States when Mexico devalued its peso.
"When Mexico devalued in '94, it cut into U.S. exports for the next six months," he said.
Brokers tied the dollar's pullback largely to technicals after a week of successively higher levels against the yen.
Last Friday, September yen rallied from a low of $0.008474 to a peak of $0.008810 to end sharply higher at $0.008766 and has not revisited those levels since.
"That's the only thing I'm thinking - that it must be a little technical correction," said one floor broker of Friday's yen advance.
"I think when I came in this morning I (expected) the dollar was going to fall," saaid Chandler, who thought the dollar likely has lost its upside momentum versus the mark.
At the same time, few looked for the Federal Reserve to raise rates at Tuesday's policymaking meeting, brokers and analysts said.

At 1010 CDT/1510 GMT, Sept yen rose $0.000048 to $0.008558, marks rose $0.0059 to $0.5502, Swiss francs added $0.0064 to $0.6676, sterling jumped $0.0206 to 1.6076, Canadian dollar firmed $0.0009 to $0.7211, Aussie dollar rose $0.0033 to $0.7450, and Mexican peso fell $0.000075 to $0.127250.
